    How a job flows

    1. Address in. Lot loads on the map, CAD record fills in the facts.
    2. Design on the lot. Tap to place patios, beds, decks and trees — measured to the foot.
    3. Show the reveal. Street-level before/after sells the job.
    4. Price it. The design totals itself into a ballpark proposal.

    The curb-appeal reveal

    Interior remodel planner

    No public database holds a home's interior blueprints — so the plan starts from a phone scan at the walkthrough (LiDAR/camera apps turn rooms into a measured floor plan in minutes) or from the CAD footprint.       Maps & satellite — full version

      This prototype designs on the built-in street map with a to-scale design layer — the drawing, measuring and pricing all work the same. The full version hooks into Google Maps + Street View with your own Google account (billing on), so any address loads its real aerial view and street photo to design over.

      Records & blueprints — half

      Public: lot lines, dimensions, square footage, year built and the footprint sketch — free from the county appraisal district. Not public: interior blueprints were never filed for most homes, so no database has them. Anyone who says otherwise is guessing.

      Interiors — the scan

      The workaround the pros use: scan the rooms with a phone at the walkthrough. LiDAR and camera apps build a measured floor plan in minutes; load it here, move finishes around, and show the customer the remodel before a single wall is touched.
